title: introduce-lightweight-presubmit-shim-and-atomic-dep-pruner
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: our presubmit lanes are noisy and heavy for small changes. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit shim that fast-paths CI for change-aware patches and an "atomic dep pruner" that trims the lockfile surface for small code edits. The goal is faster feedback (median presubmit wall time from ~13m to ~3m for typical docs/infra tweaks), fewer false CI reruns, and safer dependency churn by making lockfile updates explicit and incremental.

What this PR delivers: 
- ci/presubmit/shim: a tiny Go-based binary (90kb) that inspects the git diff and consults path-based rules to decide a minimal job set (lint-only, unit-only, or full). The shim is intended as an opt-in fastpath for changes below a configurable size threshold.
- toolchain/microimage: a minimal container image (micro-toolchain:ci-compact) with only the linters and test harness required for fast lanes. This reduces container startup and image pull time on ephemeral runners.
- scripts/dep-pruner: an "atomic dep pruner" that computes the minimal set of packages touched by a change, runs a lockfile dry-run, and emits a compact patch to the lockfile rather than a full replace. When the change touches only docs or examples, the pruner can opt to skip the lockfile touch entirely.
- ci/orchestrator: small changes to our presubmit orchestration to accept the shim's job list and to gate expanded pipelines behind an explicit consent step (comment / label) for larger changes.

Design notes: 
- Safety first: the shim never skips coverage or security scans for code that touches core runtime packages. Path rules are conservative and live in repo-owned YAML so they can be iterated without code changes.
- Incremental dep updates: the pruner produces a separate commit (automatically attached to the PR) with a deterministic header and a one-line changelog so reviewers can easily approve or reject lockfile deltas.
- Opt-in rollout: feature flag + bot comment flow; default remains full presubmit for critical directories (runtime/, serving/).

Checklist:
- [x] shim binary and tests (unit + integration against sample diffs)
- [x] microimage Dockerfile + smallsize verification on our runner fleet
- [x] dep-pruner proof-of-concept and lockfile patch generator
- [x] presubmit orchestrator wiring and feature-flag gating
- [x] docs: CONTRIBUTING.md section + internal runbook for troubleshooting fastpath cases

Testing performed:
- Benchmarked 120 small PRs (docs/examples) on ephemeral runners: median presubmit reduced from 13m to 3m; 82% of those PRs completed without touching full integration lanes.
- Verified lockfile patches for 18 representative dep changes (node/python) and ensured deterministic diffs across two CI runs.
- Runbook smoke tests: bot-driven opt-in, rollback, and forced-full-run flows validated.

Rollout plan:
1) Enable as opt-in for engineers via label / comment.
2) After one week of opt-in (monitoring acceptance/error rates), enable for docs/* and examples/* paths by default.
3) Gradually expand to other low-risk directories.

Risks & mitigations:
- Over-eager skipping: path rules are conservative; we also added a per-PR safety check that automatically escalates to full presubmit if changed file list contains runtime/ or infra/ paths.
- Lockfile divergence: pruner produces small, reviewable commits and a deterministic stamp; regressions will be caught by a lightweight lockfile-verify job that runs in the expanded lane.

Related: ENG-1223 (presubmit velocity), ENG-9801 (dep hygiene), SUP-431 (customer incident that motivated faster rollback).

Notes for reviewers: focus reviews on path-rule correctness and the safety gating (orchestrator changes). I recommend running the integration harness with a few real PR diffs listed in the runbook.

Summary of changes and why: This reduces CI noise, accelerates small edits, and introduces an audited path for lockfile changes so reviewers aren't surprised by large transitive updates. The approach favors small, deterministic changes over large lockfile churns, improving throughput for the engineering org.

ci: introduce micro-toolchain Dockerfile and CI image manifest

release_notes: Introduce opt-in lightweight presubmit shim that significantly reduces feedback time for small edits; add atomic dep pruner to create minimal lockfile patches and a compact ci micro-image to speed runner startup. Feature gated and rolled out gradually.
notes_for_follow_up: Add telemetry for skipped-presubmit rates, add an automatic revert if skipped-presubmit leads to missed regressions, and iterate on path-rule coverage for more directories.
